ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: there are 10 white islands in the figure, A is on the left side, and B is on the lower right side. From A to B in the bridge network, it can be clearly seen that there is an upper route: from A to the upper middle island, then to the upper right island, the long island on the right side, and finally to B; there is also a lower route: from A to the small island below it, then to the lower left island, the small island at the bottom near B, and finally to B. These two routes do not share the same bridge. In the lower left area of the figure, there is also a branch leading to the middle-left island and then to B, but it still belongs to the lower/B-side area. Then reason: because there exist two bridge-edge-disjoint routes from A to B, closing only 1 bridge can at most cut off one of the routes, while the other can still be passed, so at least 2 bridges need to be closed. On the other hand, closing two key bridges is enough: for example, close the bridge from the small island below A to the lower left island, and the bridge from the long island on the right side to B. In this way, all connections between the upper/left part where A is located and the lower/right part where B is located are cut off, and there is no route from A to B. Therefore, the minimum number of bridges that need to be closed is 2.
